title: Non-small-cell lung cancer
scope: Illustrative selection of four reports. These studies do not test replacing surgery with a repurposed drug. Applicability depends on the individual clinical setting.

summary.text: Surgery can be curative for selected patients with resectable NSCLC, and treatment depends on disease stage, histology and the patient's health.

The four selected reports do not establish that itraconazole or metformin can replace potentially curative surgery. The presurgical itraconazole study retained planned surgery; the other trials evaluated additional drugs in different treatment settings.

studies.title: Gerber et al. · 2020
studies.design: Short presurgical biological-effects study; 10-14 days of treatment.
studies.comparison: Measurements before and after exposure; planned surgery retained.

primary.text: Imaging, blood and tissue measurements investigated biological effects. Higher concentrations were associated with greater reductions in tumor volume and perfusion.

limitations.text: Short-term, small biological-effects study. Does not establish a survival benefit or that surgery can be omitted. Summary based on an accessible abstract.

meaning.text: Exploratory presurgical findings. Does not support replacing surgery.

studies.title: Rudin et al. · 2013
studies.population: 23 patients with previously treated metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC.
studies.design: Open-label randomized phase 2 trial; 15 combination, 8 control.
studies.comparison: Pemetrexed plus itraconazole versus pemetrexed alone.

additional.text: Median OS was 32 versus 8 months (P = .012). Reported events included grade 4 neutropenia without fever and a possibly treatment-related intratumoral bleed within 30 days after leaving the study.

limitations.text: Closed early because recruitment slowed as pemetrexed use changed. Small sample and highly unstable effect estimates; cannot establish reliable survival benefit or broad safety.

meaning.text: A preliminary signal in previously treated metastatic disease; not evidence for initial treatment of resectable disease.

studies.title: NRG LU001 · 2021
studies.population: Patients without diabetes; unresectable stage III NSCLC.
studies.design: Open-label randomized phase 2 trial. 170 enrolled; 167 eligible analyzed (86 metformin, 81 control).
studies.comparison: Chemoradiation and consolidation chemotherapy with versus without metformin.

primary.text: 1-year PFS: 51.3% with metformin versus 60.4% without it; HR 1.15 (95% CI 0.77-1.73), P = .24.

additional.text: One-year OS was similar. No significant difference in adverse events was reported.

limitations.text: Accessible abstract basis; full methods, protocol and supplement appraisal remain incomplete in this sample.

meaning.text: No demonstrated benefit from the tested metformin add-on in this population.

studies.title: OCOG ALMERA · 2021
studies.population: 54 patients without diabetes; unresected stage III NSCLC.
studies.design: Open-label randomized phase 2 trial; 26 metformin, 28 control. Recruitment stopped early.
studies.comparison: Chemoradiotherapy plus metformin versus chemoradiotherapy alone.

primary.text: 1-year composite treatment failure: 18/26 (69.2%) versus 12/28 (42.9%); P = .05. Included progression, death, or stopping trial treatment or planned evaluations for any reason.

additional.text: 1-year OS: 47.4% versus 85.2%; HR 3.80 (95% CI 1.49-9.73). Grade >=3 adverse events: 14/26 (53.8%) versus 7/28 (25.0%). These were all-cause events, not all attributed to metformin.

limitations.text: Small sample, open-label design and treatment imbalances limit interpretation.

meaning.text: Unfavorable outcomes argue against this anticancer add-on in the tested setting.

safety.text: The U.S. capsule label warns about heart failure, serious liver toxicity and consequential drug interactions, including contraindicated combinations involving CYP3A4 substrates.
safety.label: Itraconazole

safety.text: The metformin trials studied an anticancer add-on in people without diabetes. Their findings do not instruct patients to change an existing diabetes prescription. Discuss current medicines with the care team.
safety.label: Existing metformin use

questions: Which studies, if any, match my stage, histology, biomarkers and treatment history?
If a repurposed approach is unsuitable, is the reason evidence quality, applicability, safety or another concern?
Would a specialist opinion or trial inquiry be appropriate within the recommended treatment timeline?

coverage: Selected-source sample of four reports from 2013, 2020 and 2021. This is not a systematic review or a comprehensive search through the check date. Two summaries use abstracts and two use accessible full-text sections. Complete scientific appraisals and independent clinical review remain pending. Article PDFs are not reproduced.
